Subject: Production p95 spike + 5xx surge — Orpheus private VPC

Markus,

We started seeing a major regression on our private VPC deployment Friday night after a scheduled model rollout (model v2.3). Since ~02:00 PDT we've observed p95 latency climb from ~320ms to sustained ~1.6-1.9s and a spike in 5xx responses (mostly 502/504). Error-rate peaked at ~9% for a 30 minute window; now it's hovering 2-3% but still unacceptable.

We've attached a trimmed set of orchesterd logs and a trace file (orchard-logs-20280605.tar.gz, trace-20280605.json). Key facts:
- Private cluster: orpheus-prod-vpc (us-west-2 region)
- Deployment: custom runtime image built 2028-06-04 (we followed your rollout guide)
- Recent change: model pin to v2.3 + KV cache TTL cut from 600s -> 120s in the deploy manifest (orc-deploy-manifest.yaml)

This is live production (our checkout flow). We need an urgent triage and either a mitigation path or rollback instructions. Please advise next steps and ETA for a fix.

--
Alex Ramirez
Head of Platform, Orpheus Labs

Subject: Re: Production p95 spike + 5xx surge — Orpheus private VPC (initial findings)

Thanks — I've pulled the traces and logs you attached and started a quick correlation with our runtime telemetry. High-level findings:
- p95 climbed from baseline ~320ms to peaks ~1.8s after the v2.3 rollout window.
- 5xxs correlate with worker process OOMs and a sustained queue backlog on the mini-batcher component.
- KV cache miss rate jumped ~4x after the TTL reduction; cold prefixes are causing repeated KV recompute and longer decode paths.
- We also see an uptick in mmap ENOMEM hazards on one host (node-07) around the same timeframe — likely an interaction between our memory reclamation path and your runtime image's allocator.

Immediate recommended actions (order of preference / least disruption first):
A) Increase KV cache TTL from 120s -> 600s (matches prior config) — expected improvement to p95 within 10-20m as hot prefixes rewarm.
B) Reduce max_batch_size from 8 -> 4 for the decode worker pools to lower tail latency; this will slightly increase per-token cost but drops p95 quickly.
C) Pin model back to v2.2 if A/B shows no improvement within 45m.
D) Apply a runtime patch (non-breaking, small allocator tweak) to node-07 to avoid transient ENOMEM — requires rolling restart of that host (target 15m host restart, can be done one host at a time).

I can push A+B immediately if you give permission. If you prefer rollback (C) I can coordinate the pin and traffic shift. ETA for A+B rollout + metrics check: ~30–45 minutes.

Logs snippet (from trace-20280605.json):
[2028-06-05T01:58:33Z] worker-7 decode: enqueue latency 1.12s; kv-cache-miss=true
[2028-06-05T01:59:10Z] node-07: mmap ENOMEM (reclaimed 0 KB)
[2028-06-05T02:05:02Z] http-502: upstream read timeout on worker-7

Proposed immediate ops: you (Orpheus) approve config change A and B, we push changes to private control plane and monitor for 30m. If no regression, keep config; otherwise rollback to v2.2 and open a postmortem.

-Jonas Weber
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alex — quick update and plan of record following the huddle:

What we did (10:10–11:20 PDT):
- Applied config change A: KV cache TTL set back to 600s.
- Applied config change B: max_batch_size reduced to 4 for decode workers.
- Monitored metrics on both control plane and your prometheus (we pulled aggregated p95 and 5xx dashboards).

Immediate results (observed by 11:10 PDT):
- p95 moved from ~1.8s -> ~420ms within ~25 minutes.
- 5xx rate dropped from 9% peak to 0.6% within 30 minutes.
- node-07 showed fewer mmap ENOMEM events post-change but we still recommend the targeted runtime patch and rolling restart.

Next steps (next 3 hours):
1) Jonas to push the allocator patch and perform a rolling restart of node-07 (one host at a time) — ETA 2 hours. We'll coordinate a 5-minute traffic pause per host; we'll keep you informed 10 minutes prior.
2) If metrics regress after patch, we will perform pinned rollback to v2.2 (pre-approved by Alex).
3) Lauren will draft the incident summary and goodwill proposal (we'll finalize after full remediation).

Huddle: We scheduled a short follow-up huddle at 14:30 PDT (calendar link: https://cal.redwood.ai/huddle/orpheus-20280605).

Please keep traffic at ~40% until we confirm post-restart telemetry. If you'd like us to failover to Redwood-hosted (managed) endpoints temporarily, we can coordinate that as a fallback.

Attachments pushed to shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdEfGh (logs, traces, runbook).

Thanks again for the quick coordination — we'll keep this thread updated and follow up with a full postmortem within 48 hours.
